page.title: How to run your first conference

text.content: Getting started

rich_text.plain_text: Getting started

text.content: Invite good speakers. Speakers are what draw the crowd.

rich_text.plain_text: Invite good speakers. Speakers are what draw the crowd.

text.content: Pick a date and a venue.

rich_text.plain_text: Pick a date and a venue.

text.content: Set up a website. Copy existing conference websites. Have speaker faces. Have a date.

rich_text.plain_text: Set up a website. Copy existing conference websites. Have speaker faces. Have a date.

text.content: Copy a ticketing system. Luma will do in a pinch.

rich_text.plain_text: Copy a ticketing system. Luma will do in a pinch.

text.content: Have some kind of way of tracking speaker reachouts and attendees. Highly recommend Airtable for this.

rich_text.plain_text: Have some kind of way of tracking speaker reachouts and attendees. Highly recommend Airtable for this.

text.content: Create a conference calendar. Airtable is reasonable.

rich_text.plain_text: Create a conference calendar. Airtable is reasonable.

text.content: There isn’t a great conference app. Swapcard is eh. You can maybe vibecode one.

rich_text.plain_text: There isn’t a great conference app. Swapcard is eh. You can maybe vibecode one.

text.content: The people

rich_text.plain_text: The people

text.content: Events are mostly about the quality of the people who show up.

rich_text.plain_text: Events are mostly about the quality of the people who show up.

text.content: Spend way more time than seems reasonable hand-inviting people who would be good. Don’t just blast group chats, go the extra mile, write a personalized message indicating why they’re welcome.

rich_text.plain_text: Spend way more time than seems reasonable hand-inviting people who would be good. Don’t just blast group chats, go the extra mile, write a personalized message indicating why they’re welcome.

text.content: Conferences are a great excuse to reach out to people you admire online, and ask them to come to your thing. Cold outreach can be surprisingly good.

rich_text.plain_text: Conferences are a great excuse to reach out to people you admire online, and ask them to come to your thing. Cold outreach can be surprisingly good.

text.content: Think about where the people who you want to come hang out, and market there. Post links, make flyers, give talks, etc.

rich_text.plain_text: Think about where the people who you want to come hang out, and market there. Post links, make flyers, give talks, etc.

text.content: Referrals, of course. Conferences are more fun with friends.

rich_text.plain_text: Referrals, of course. Conferences are more fun with friends.

text.content: Ask the speakers to help with promotion, to their audiences

rich_text.plain_text: Ask the speakers to help with promotion, to their audiences

text.content: You can set up an application process if you’re trying to curate a premier experience, and maybe get a prestige boost. Beware, though; application process is soulsucking. So ideally you can get away with just positive selection (promoting in the right places) rather than negative (filtering out people you don’t want)

text.content: Engineering great experiences

rich_text.plain_text: Engineering great experiences

text.content: The best moments come from attendees making things happen. Unconference sessions, singalongs, games, lightning talks, etc.

rich_text.plain_text: The best moments come from attendees making things happen. Unconference sessions, singalongs, games, lightning talks, etc.

text.content: Booths are another way to do this. Career fairs, night markets, basically structures where there’s supply and demand. (Markets are beautiful.)

rich_text.plain_text: Booths are another way to do this. Career fairs, night markets, basically structures where there’s supply and demand. (Markets are beautiful.)

text.content: Hallway track is one of the best parts, so give people permission to do hallway track, aka wandering around.

rich_text.plain_text: Hallway track is one of the best parts, so give people permission to do hallway track, aka wandering around.

text.content: 1:1s can be really good. (Though, you can go too far — see EAG.)

rich_text.plain_text: 1:1s can be really good. (Though, you can go too far — see EAG.)

text.content: Provide food. This keeps people hanging around, rather than dispersing

rich_text.plain_text: Provide food. This keeps people hanging around, rather than dispersing

text.content: Talks… are a bit maligned nowadays, I think they’re actually still pretty great. Underappreciated features of talks: they force busy speakers to make their recent thoughts legible to others. They act as a batsignal to bring together people who care about specific topics.

rich_text.plain_text: Talks… are a bit maligned nowadays, I think they’re actually still pretty great. Underappreciated features of talks: they force busy speakers to make their recent thoughts legible to others. They act as a batsignal to bring together people who care about specific topics.

text.content: I think the ideal thing is something like 1h slots. 20min talk (people don’t actually want to listen to long talks); 20min Q&A (moderated or audience Qs); 20 min office hours (aka give most people permission to leave, and then the remaining 10 people who care a lot get individual time with the speaker)

rich_text.plain_text: I think the ideal thing is something like 1h slots. 20min talk (people don’t actually want to listen to long talks); 20min Q&A (moderated or audience Qs); 20 min office hours (aka give most people permission to leave, and then the remaining 10 people who care a lot get individual time with the speaker)

text.content: Build in transition time, eg start everything 5 minutes after the hour

rich_text.plain_text: Build in transition time, eg start everything 5 minutes after the hour

text.content: You can do fireside chats as an alternative to entice people who are too busy to prepare a talk. (but, those are less good than actual prepped talks.)

rich_text.plain_text: You can do fireside chats as an alternative to entice people who are too busy to prepare a talk. (but, those are less good than actual prepped talks.)

text.content: Have, not just a diversity of talk topics, but also a diversity of experiences people can opt into. Some for introverts, some for extraverts; some for newcomers, some for enmeshed individuals.

rich_text.plain_text: Have, not just a diversity of talk topics, but also a diversity of experiences people can opt into. Some for introverts, some for extraverts; some for newcomers, some for enmeshed individuals.

text.content: Financials

rich_text.plain_text: Financials

text.content: Expect to lose money on your first conference.

rich_text.plain_text: Expect to lose money on your first conference.

text.content: Definitely have early bird pricing, you want to encourage early commitment. Raise prices and use that as an excuse to do more marketing (”prices going up soon!”)

rich_text.plain_text: Definitely have early bird pricing, you want to encourage early commitment. Raise prices and use that as an excuse to do more marketing (”prices going up soon!”)

text.content: Have a tier where people can pay a lot — helps to anchor to higher amounts. Give them some nice perks (special badge, VIP dinner are cheap to provide but valuable to sponsors)

rich_text.plain_text: Have a tier where people can pay a lot — helps to anchor to higher amounts. Give them some nice perks (special badge, VIP dinner are cheap to provide but valuable to sponsors)

text.content: Later on, you can make a lot of money on sponsorships. There’s an entire art to this. Sponsors usually want some combination of brand, marketing, recruiting, and largess (to support the community) — ask about their specific goals.

rich_text.plain_text: Later on, you can make a lot of money on sponsorships. There’s an entire art to this. Sponsors usually want some combination of brand, marketing, recruiting, and largess (to support the community) — ask about their specific goals.

text.content: You’ll probably spend the most money on the venue, then food, then a bunch of random other expenses.

rich_text.plain_text: You’ll probably spend the most money on the venue, then food, then a bunch of random other expenses.

text.content: Print good swag, it’s worth it. Your event will then live on in people’s everyday wardrobes.

rich_text.plain_text: Print good swag, it’s worth it. Your event will then live on in people’s everyday wardrobes.

text.content: Logistics

rich_text.plain_text: Logistics

text.content: In planning, make sure you agree on shared systems: CRMs, internal chat, email (try a shared email system like Missive)

rich_text.plain_text: In planning, make sure you agree on shared systems: CRMs, internal chat, email (try a shared email system like Missive)

text.content: Have good day-of comms, like a Discord/Slack.

rich_text.plain_text: Have good day-of comms, like a Discord/Slack.

text.content: Each evening, run through the game plan for the next day with your staff

rich_text.plain_text: Each evening, run through the game plan for the next day with your staff

text.content: Managing a volunteer team — find leaders who’ve done this before, run a training session

rich_text.plain_text: Managing a volunteer team — find leaders who’ve done this before, run a training session

text.content: You don’t need to be amazing at public speaking (I sure am not) but you do have to take some charge.

rich_text.plain_text: You don’t need to be amazing at public speaking (I sure am not) but you do have to take some charge.

text.content: To get a crowd to quiet down, I like “if you can hear me clap once”, then twice, etc. By 3, everyone’s watching you.

rich_text.plain_text: To get a crowd to quiet down, I like “if you can hear me clap once”, then twice, etc. By 3, everyone’s watching you.

text.content: Get ops experience by volunteering at other conferences.

rich_text.plain_text: Get ops experience by volunteering at other conferences.

text.content: Also just attend some, and take notes about what was good and what was bad

rich_text.plain_text: Also just attend some, and take notes about what was good and what was bad

text.content: Feedback session: copy EAG, make everyone fill it out at the end, otherwise you get a lot less feedback

rich_text.plain_text: Feedback session: copy EAG, make everyone fill it out at the end, otherwise you get a lot less feedback

text.content: Make sure to have a section where people can write nice things about the event. Good for you to read later, good testimonials to market

rich_text.plain_text: Make sure to have a section where people can write nice things about the event. Good for you to read later, good testimonials to market

text.content: Even better, get them to send nice messages to each other. Sometimes these are called “affirmations” or “kudos”
